title: What training does a preventive controls qualified individual need under FSMA?
description: 21 CFR 117.180 and 117.4 explained: what a PCQI must do, the standardized curriculum or job experience routes, worker hygiene training and records to keep.
shortAnswer: Under the FDA Preventive Controls for Human Food rule, 21 CFR 117.180 requires a preventive controls qualified individual (PCQI) to prepare or oversee the food safety plan, validation, record review and reanalysis, qualified through training at least equivalent to an FDA recognized standardized curriculum or through job experience. Separately, 21 CFR 117.4 requires every worker to be qualified and trained in food hygiene and food safety, with training records kept for at least two years.
keyTakeaways: 21 CFR 117.126(a)(2) requires the food safety plan to be prepared, or its preparation overseen, by one or more preventive controls qualified individuals.

Under 117.180(c)(1), a PCQI qualifies by completing training in risk based preventive controls at least equivalent to a standardized curriculum recognized as adequate by FDA, or through job experience.
117.180(d) requires PCQI training records showing the date, the type of training and the person trained.

117.4(b)(2) requires all personnel who manufacture, process, pack or hold food to be trained in food hygiene and food safety, including employee health and personal hygiene, and 117.4(d) requires records of that training.
117.315(a)(1) requires records under part 117 to be kept at the facility for at least 2 years after preparation.
jurisdiction: United States (federal): Food Safety Modernization Act (FSMA); 21 CFR part 117, Current Good Manufacturing Practice, Hazard Analysis, and Risk-Based Preventive Controls for Human Food
appliesTo: Domestic and foreign food facilities required to register under section 415 of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (subpart C preventive controls)
All establishments that manufacture, process, pack or hold human food (subpart B current good manufacturing practice, including 117.4)
Plant management, supervisors and every individual handling food
Owners, operators or agents in charge of covered facilities

sections.heading: Which facilities must have a PCQI?

blocks.text: Facilities subject to the preventive controls requirements in subpart C of 21 CFR part 117 need a PCQI. [FDA](https://www.fda.gov/food/food-safety-modernization-act-fsma/fsma-final-rule-preventive-controls-human-food) states that domestic and foreign food facilities required to register under section 415 of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act must comply with the requirements for risk based preventive controls, subject to exemptions such as those for qualified facilities.

The qualification rules in 117.4 reach further. FDA notes that applicability of the current good manufacturing practice requirements does not depend on whether a facility must register, so a non registered establishment that manufactures, processes, packs or holds food still has to qualify and train its workers. Compliance dates were staggered: September 19, 2016 for large businesses, September 18, 2017 for small businesses, and September 17, 2018 for very small businesses; all have passed.

A qualified facility, defined in [117.3](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/21/117.3) to include a very small business, is subject to modified requirements rather than the full food safety plan. It must keep records supporting that status for as long as needed during the applicable calendar year.

The PCQI must perform or oversee the technical core of the food safety plan. [21 CFR 117.180(a)](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/21/117.180) lists those activities, and 117.126(a)(2) assigns plan preparation to one or more PCQIs.

items: Preparation of the food safety plan, which under 117.126(b) contains the hazard analysis, preventive controls, supply chain program, recall plan, and monitoring, corrective action and verification procedures.
Written justification for validation timeframes that exceed the default and determinations that validation is not required.
Reanalysis of the food safety plan.

blocks.text: The facility can use more than one PCQI, and part 117 does not state that the PCQI must be an employee. What matters for an inspector is that each listed activity was done or overseen by someone who meets the qualification test, and that the facility can prove it.

sections.heading: How does someone qualify as a PCQI?

blocks.text: There are two routes: training at least equivalent to an FDA recognized standardized curriculum, or job experience. The definition in 117.3 and the qualification rule in 117.180(c)(1) use the same wording.

blocks.title: Primary text: 21 CFR 117.3
blocks.text: "Preventive controls qualified individual means a qualified individual who has successfully completed training in the development and application of risk-based preventive controls at least equivalent to that received under a standardized curriculum recognized as adequate by FDA or is otherwise qualified through job experience to develop and apply a food safety system."

FDA's partner for the standardized curriculum is the [Food Safety Preventive Controls Alliance (FSPCA)](https://www.fda.gov/food/food-safety-modernization-act-fsma/food-safety-preventive-controls-alliance), which FDA describes as developing a standardized hazard analysis and preventive controls course and distance education modules for industry and regulators. The regulation does not require the FSPCA course by name; it requires training "at least equivalent" to the recognized curriculum.

The job experience route is legitimate but harder to evidence. A facility relying on it should document the specific food safety system work the person has done, over what period, and how it maps to the activities in 117.180(a). A structured [competency assessment](/glossary/competency-assessment) against the curriculum's topics is one way to make that case reviewable.

sections.heading: What does 21 CFR 117.4 require for every worker?

blocks.text: Every individual who manufactures, processes, packs or holds food must be a qualified individual and must be trained in food hygiene and food safety. [21 CFR 117.4](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/21/117.4) sets three layers.

blocks.caption: Qualification layers in 21 CFR 117.4 (as at November 2026)
head: Paragraph
Who
Requirement
rows: Each individual engaged in manufacturing, processing, packing or holding
Have the education, training or experience (or a combination) needed to do so cleanly and safely, as appropriate to assigned duties
Receive training in the principles of food hygiene and food safety, including the importance of employee health and personal hygiene, as appropriate
Clearly assigned responsibility for ensuring compliance, with the education, training or experience needed to supervise
Establish and maintain records documenting the training required by 117.4(b)(2)

blocks.text: Under 117.4(a), responsibility sits with management of the establishment for subpart B and with the owner, operator or agent in charge of a facility for subparts C to G. This makes worker hygiene training a management obligation that inspectors can check independently of the PCQI's work. For pharmaceutical and dietary supplement contexts, compare [FDA GMP personnel training requirements](/regulations/fda-gmp-personnel-training-requirements).

sections.heading: What records will an FDA investigator expect?

blocks.text: An investigator will expect to see who the PCQI is, how that person qualified, and that workers were trained and the training recorded. Under 117.315(a)(1), all part 117 records must be kept at the plant or facility for at least 2 years after the date they were prepared. The table is illustrative.

blocks.caption: Illustrative part 117 training obligation map
head: Obligation
Role
Frequency
Evidence an investigator would expect
rows: Prepare or oversee food safety plan (117.126(a)(2))
Course certificate, or written record of job experience mapped to 117.180(a)
Record with date, type of training and person trained
Written assignment of responsibility; qualification record
Records available on site for at least 2 years

blocks.text: For the general method of retention schedules, see [how long to keep training records](/guides/how-long-to-keep-training-records). For farms rather than facilities, the parallel federal rule is the [FSMA produce safety rule worker training](/regulations/fsma-produce-safety-rule-worker-training) requirement.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry can structure the 117.180(a) activities as a competence framework, so a PCQI qualified through job experience is assessed against the same outcomes as a course graduate, with the evidence held in a form an investigator can review. See [audit evidence](/platform/audit-evidence).

faqs.q: Does a PCQI have to take the FSPCA course?
faqs.a: No. 21 CFR 117.180(c)(1) requires training at least equivalent to a standardized curriculum recognized as adequate by FDA, or qualification through job experience. The FSPCA course is the curriculum FDA supported, but equivalence or experience are permitted, provided the facility can document them.

faqs.q: Must the PCQI be an employee of the facility?
faqs.a: The regulation requires that the listed activities be performed or overseen by a person who meets the PCQI definition; it does not say that person must be on the payroll. Whoever acts as PCQI, the facility must keep the 117.180(d) training record showing date, type of training and the person trained.

faqs.q: How long must FSMA training records be kept?
faqs.a: 21 CFR 117.315(a)(1) requires all records required by part 117 to be retained at the plant or facility for at least 2 years after the date they were prepared. That covers both PCQI training records under 117.180(d) and worker training records under 117.4(d).

faqs.q: Does 117.4 apply if my facility does not need to register with FDA?
faqs.a: Yes, for the current good manufacturing practice provisions. FDA states that applicability of the CGMPs does not depend on whether a facility is required to register. 117.4(a)(1) makes management responsible for ensuring individuals subject to subparts B and F are qualified.
